One still, gray day, two tired friends, Ivan Ivanych, a veterinary surgeon, and Burkin, a high school teacher, were walking across wide fields that seemed to have no end. <break time="0.8s" /> Far away stood the windmills of the village they were heading for, and the whole quiet countryside lay before them, so lovely that both men felt a deep love for it. <break time="0.8s" /> Burkin reminded his friend of a story he had promised to tell, but just as Ivan Ivanych was about to begin, a heavy rain started to fall. <break time="0.8s" /> Since the rain showed no sign of stopping, Burkin suggested that they take shelter at the estate of their friend Alyohin, which was close by. <break time="0.8s" /> When they reached the estate, soaked and muddy, they found a gloomy scene, with the mill wheel turning noisily and wet horses standing with drooping heads. <break time="0.8s" /> Everything was damp and dreary, and the two travelers, tired and cold, walked in silence as though they were angry with each other. <break time="0.8s" /> Alyohin, a tall, stout man of about forty, came out to meet them, covered in dust from his work in the barn, and was clearly delighted to have visitors. <break time="0.8s" /> He looked more like a scholar or an artist than a landowner, and he confessed that he had scarcely washed himself since the spring. <break time="0.8s" /> Then a young maid named Pelageya appeared with towels and soap, and she was so beautiful that both guests stopped short and glanced at each other.
